Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law · Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

session noun

a sitting of a council, court or senate

also sessions, sitting, in session, court session, session of parliament

classical

Cic. de Or. 3.121: pōmerīdiāna sessiō (Lewis & Short)
Dig. 38.15.2.1: diēs sessiōnum, of a court (Lewis & Short)

sessiō, sessiōnis f.

noun, third declension

a sitting, a session

Literally the act of sitting, and so a seat; Cicero uses it of an afternoon’s sitting for discussion, and of idle sitting about (sessiō Capitōlīna, Att. 14.14.2, Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • senātus, senātūs m. — a sitting of the senate

    noun, fourth declension · also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 12.25a.1 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 180, 376: senate session, senātus; to hold a session, senātum habēre

    The senate itself and its meeting: senātum habēre, to hold a session; senātum vocāre, to call one (Traupman).

  • cōnsessus, cōnsessūs m. — an assembly sitting together

    noun, fourth declension · also used · classical · Cic. Sen. 63: magnō cōnsessū

    The people seated in a court, a theatre or at the games, rather than the time they sit (Lewis & Short). For a period given to an activity, such as a training session or a lesson, Latin names the activity (see exercise, lesson).

Examples

  • eō diē nōn fuit senātus neque posterō

    there was no session of the senate that day, nor the nextCic. Fam. 12.25a.1 (Lewis & Short)

See also meeting, attend, lesson, exercise.
